title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES COMBINED CONVOCATION CEREMONY OF 18 NIFT CAMPUSES
subtitle: STUDENTS SHOULD MAINTAIN A GLOBAL OUTLOOK WHILE REMAINING FIRMLY CONNECTED TO THEIR ROOTS AND THE CORE VALUES OF OUR CULTURE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the combined convocation ceremony of 18 National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) Campuses in New Delhi today (August 31, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the textile and apparel sector is not just a part of our cultural heritage, but it has also been the backbone of the livelihoods of millions of people. If the traditional artisans receive the support and guidance, it will encourage their next generations to remain engaged in this profession with pride and confidence. She was happy to note that various NIFT centres have implemented programmes like the 'Craft Cluster Initiative' to acquaint weavers and artisans in their respective regions with modern techniques in the textile and apparel sector and to connect them with markets.
The President said that today, our country is expanding its role on the global stage with far greater confidence than ever before. Fashion Technology is also a field with immense potential to enhance India’s global footprint. She urged graduating students to seize this opportunity. She said that in this endeavour, students should maintain a global outlook while remaining firmly connected to their roots and the core values of our culture. By doing so, they will not only become successful professionals but also contribute to the preservation and enrichment of India’s cultural heritage.
The President said that students should create world-class products and brands, but they should also ensure that these are eco-friendly. She stated that the use of locally available raw materials for their products will be a significant step towards environmental conservation. Remnants should not be discarded as waste; they can be given a new form, new utility, and new value. She was happy to note that NIFT’s policymakers have accorded significant importance to sustainability and social responsibility within the institute's strategic plan. She expressed confidence that NIFT will take effective steps to make circular economy practices widespread and beneficial, aligned with its efforts toward a sustainable future in the textile and apparel sector.
The President said that the youth will play a pivotal role in achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. She underlined that the nation has high expectations from talented young students of prestigious institutes like NIFT. She urged them to contribute to building a society where every citizen has a fair opportunity to participate in the nation's progress. She said that their success lies in their efforts to help artisans enhance their productivity and income while preserving the authentic identity of their craft.

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology and inaugurates Confluence 3.0
subtitle:
Vice President calls for research-driven higher education and stronger industry-academia linkages

Keralam must focus on high-tech industries to create jobs and enable reverse migration: Vice President

“We just cannot produce graduates; we have to understand the demands of the market”: Vice President

“Say No to Drugs”: Vice President urges students to protect their dreams and aspirations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology (RSET) and inaugurated Confluence 3.0, an Industry-Academia Summit focused on “India, Impact of AI”, in Kochi.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology (RSET) and inaugurated Confluence 3.0, an Industry-Academia Summit focused on “India, Impact of AI”, in Kochi today.

Highlighting Keralam’s achievements in literacy, social development and human capital, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Rajagiri has contributed not only to producing technocrats but also leaders in public life. He congratulated the institution on completing 25 years and appreciated its commitment to combining values with technological excellence.
Recalling the contribution of the Carmelites of Mary Immaculate (CMI) and the legacy of Saint Kuriakose Elias Chavara, he highlighted their pioneering efforts in democratising education, promoting women’s education and adult literacy, and ensuring that poverty and hunger did not become barriers to learning.
Emphasising the changing demands of the technology-driven world, the Vice President said education cannot be limited to degrees. “We just cannot produce graduates; we have to understand the demands of the market,” he said, calling for greater emphasis on research, innovation and problem-solving.
Commending Confluence 3.0, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said stronger industry-academia partnerships are essential to make Bharat a global hub for technology and start-ups. He called for innovative teaching, interdisciplinary research, responsible use of AI and meaningful international collaborations while remaining rooted in Bharat’s values.
Referring to China’s transformation over the past few decades, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said its progress demonstrates the importance of sustained investment in higher education, research and innovation. He urged Keralam to strengthen research-oriented higher education and create an ecosystem that promotes innovation.
Appealing to the Chief Minister, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Keralam’s limited land availability and high land costs make large traditional industries challenging, and urged a greater focus on high-tech and knowledge-based industries. He said Keralam’s strong educational base and talent pool can attract high-technology enterprises, create local employment, reduce migration and enable reverse migration.
The Vice President made a strong appeal to young people to “Say No to Drugs.” Recalling his mother’s advice during his childhood, he said temporary pleasures can destroy great hopes and goals, and urged students to use their capabilities for the betterment of themselves, society and humanity.
The Vice President also laid the foundation stone for the Administrative Block of Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology, marking another milestone in the institution’s journey of growth and academic excellence.
The programme was attended by the Governor of Keralam, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chief Minister of Keralam, Shri V. D. Satheesan; Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas and Tourism, Shri Suresh Gopi; Minister for Higher Education,Government of Keralam, Shri Roji M. John; and other dignitaries, including the management, faculty and students of RSET.

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends Fisheries Outreach Programme in Agatti, Lakshadweep
subtitle:
Vice President releases “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development in Lakshadweep

Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision is driving India’s Blue Revolution; Lakshadweep poised for new era of fisheries-led growth: Vice President

‘Blue Revolution will be as transformative as Green and White Revolutions’: Vice President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 3:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the Fisheries Outreach Programme at Agatti, Lakshadweep, and released “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031”, the Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development. He also distributed various government benefits and assistance to beneficiaries from the fisheries sector.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Fisheries Outreach Programme at Agatti, Lakshadweep, and released “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031”, the Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development today.
The Vice President described the occasion as a historic day…
pic.twitter.com/1U9CXDKoVf
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
August 31, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President described the occasion as a historic day for Lakshadweep and a new milestone in India’s Blue Revolution. Referring to the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said that the blue chakra in India’s national flag represents the potential of the Blue Revolution and the ocean economy. He noted that under the Prime Minister’s leadership, India’s fisheries and aquaculture sector has emerged as a major sunrise sector of the economy.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the Government is transforming governance by taking support and schemes directly to fishing communities, rather than waiting for people to approach the Government. He highlighted that fisheries development projects worth over ₹62 crore have been approved for Lakshadweep under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
Highlighting Lakshadweep’s vast maritime potential, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the islands have an estimated fisheries potential of over one lakh tonnes, including around 94,000 tonnes of tuna and tuna-like species. He emphasised the need to harness this potential scientifically and sustainably while ensuring greater prosperity for island communities.
The Vice President also highlighted India’s growing seafood exports, which crossed ₹73,000 crore in the last financial year and reached more than 120 countries. He said initiatives relating to the EEZ and High Seas would further strengthen India’s fisheries sector and India’s presence in global seafood markets.
Emphasising sustainability, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for responsible fishing, conservation of marine resources and firm action against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. He urged the youth to view fisheries not merely as an inherited occupation but as a modern profession driven by science, technology, innovation and global opportunities.
Drawing parallels with the Green and White Revolutions, the Vice President said the Blue Revolution has the potential to similarly transform the lives of fishing communities. He urged all stakeholders to work together to make India’s Blue Economy a powerful pillar of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The programme was attended by Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh; Administrator of Lakshadweep Shri Praful K. Patel; Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel; and Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, among others.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan arrived in Agatti, Lakshadweep, on his maiden visit to the Lakshadweep Islands today.
He was warmly received by Shri Praful K. Patel, Administrator, Union Territory of Lakshadweep, and was also accorded a Guard of Honour on arrival.

title: Meeting of Prime Minister with the President of the Russian Federation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today met the President of the Russian Federation, H.E. Vladimir Putin, in Bishkek, on the margins of the 26th SCO Summit. This was their first meeting this year. The two leaders had earlier met in Delhi for the 23rd Annual Summit in December 2025.
The two leaders reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation in a range of fields, including political, economic, defence, energy, space, mobility and people-to-people ties. They welcomed the outcome of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic and Cultural matters, which was held on 24 August 2026 in Moscow.
The leaders exchanged views on India-Russia engagement in the multilateral arena, in particular in BRICS under India’s Chairship for 2026. They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. Prime Minister reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts.
The two leaders agreed to remain engaged to further strengthen the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries, which continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties.
Prime Minister stated that he looks forward to welcoming President Putin in India for the 18th BRICS Summit on 12-13 September 2026.

title: NHRIMH Kottayam Organises National Seminar on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Homoeopathy
subtitle: Seminar explores AI-enabled clinical decision support, personalised care and ethical frameworks in Homoeopathic research
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Homoeopathy Research Institute in Mental Health (NHRIMH), Kottayam, under the Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH), Ministry of Ayush organised a National Seminar on
“Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Clinical Practice and Homoeopathy”
today at the NHRIMH Auditorium, Kottayam. Organised under the theme
“Where Intelligence Meets Compassion”
, the seminar brought together experts, academicians, researchers, clinicians, practitioners and students to deliberate on the emerging applications of AI in healthcare and Homoeopathic research.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, addressed the programme virtually. In his address, the Minister highlighted the growing relevance of Artificial Intelligence in healthcare and the importance of informed discussions on its responsible application, particularly in the field of Homoeopathy.
The inaugural session was addressed by Dr. Subhash Kaushik, Director General, CCRH.  He emphasised the need for researchers and academicians to understand both the capabilities and ethical dimensions of AI to ensure its responsible application in healthcare and research.
The deliberations underscored that the adoption of AI in healthcare must be supported by human oversight, scientific validation, data credibility and appropriate ethical safeguards.
On the occasion, nine MoUs were signed with Homoeopathic Medical Colleges and Hospitals to strengthen academic collaboration in psychiatry and mental health. An MoU was also signed with Sevabharathi, Ettumanoor, for interdisciplinary research and institutional collaboration.
Dr. Debadatta Nayak, Assistant Director (Homoeopathy) and Officer-in-Charge, NHRIMH, said that representatives from around 12 Homoeopathic Medical Colleges across India, along with practitioners and faculty members from Kerala, participated in the seminar, providing a platform for academic exchange on AI in healthcare and Homoeopathy.
Dr. K. C. Muraleedharan, Deputy Director General, CCRH, Dr. Janardhanan Nair, Former President, Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB), National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH), and Prof. (Dr.) Eswara Das, Chairman, Regional Scientific Advisory Committee, NHRIMH, Kottayam, also addressed the gathering. The technical programme comprised four sessions focusing on AI in clinical decision support, applications of AI in Homoeopathy, and ethical aspects of AI in clinico-fundamental research.
The seminar reflects the commitment of CCRH and NHRIMH, Kottayam towards scientific innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration and responsible adoption of emerging technologies in Homoeopathic research and clinical practice. The initiative is expected to further strengthen academic and research networks and facilitate informed dialogue on the opportunities and challenges presented by AI in healthcare and Homoeopathy.

The meeting, building on the strong political momentum led by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and President Luiz Inácio Lula De Silva, reflected on the strong institutional framework underpinning the India-Brazil Strategic Partnership and the shared commitment of both sides to deepen strategic and economic ties.
Commerce Secretary also met Minister of Development, Industry, Commerce and Services, Government of Brazil, Mr. Marcio Elias Rosa, to discuss further deepening bilateral trade and investment ties and enhancing economic cooperation in priority sectors. Bilateral trade between India and Brazil has shown consistent growth, reaching USD 15.07 billion in 2025–26. Recognising the complementarities between the two economies, both sides reaffirmed their shared objective of expanding bilateral trade to USD 30 billion by 2030 through a more diversified, balanced and sustainable partnership, particularly in pharmaceuticals, chemicals, engineering goods and machinery.
During the meetings, both sides reviewed progress on the India–MERCOSUR Terms of Reference. The India–MERCOSUR Preferential Trade Agreement offers considerable scope for expansion and modernisation. With India-MERCOSUR bilateral trade reaching USD 20.84 billion in 2025, both sides committed to early finalisation of the Terms of Reference.
Significant progress was also made in facilitating market access for Indian pharmaceutical products. The CDSCO–ANVISA MoU signed in February 2026 provides an important institutional foundation for deeper cooperation in health and pharmaceuticals. India emphasised the need for supporting more predictable regulatory pathways and facilitating greater market access. India can contribute to the availability of affordable, quality medicines and strengthen efforts towards more accessible healthcare.
On agriculture, the discussions advanced work on priority phytosanitary requests on key products of interest, while laying out a clear agenda to take forward the technical processes towards reciprocal market access concessions in a time-bound manner. The discussions also noted the encouraging progress on mutual recognition of Electronic Certificates of Origin and on Cooperation in MSMEs, Entrepreneurship and Crafts, terming them significant steps towards greater trade facilitation and easing barriers to trade for business-to-business engagement.
Both sides reaffirmed close coordination on multilateral issues, including under BRICS, the G20 and the WTO, in support of an open, inclusive and development-oriented multilateral system. India appreciated Brazil’s engagement in advancing the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2030 and the GVC Action Plan 2026–2030. Brazil congratulated India on its work during its BRICS Presidency, particularly initiatives such as the BRICS Startup Knowledge Hub and BRICS Business Incubator.
As a part of the bilateral engagement, an India-Brazil High Level Business Reception was also organised in Brasilia with participation from leading business representatives and industry stakeholders from both countries. Commerce Secretary led the Indian business delegation comprising over 25 Indian businesses, including representatives from Kirloskar Group, UPL, Aditya Birla Group, amongst others. The Business Reception served as an important platform for exploring new avenues of collaboration in sectors such as critical minerals, renewable energy, agri-business, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, digital services, logistics and advanced manufacturing. Both sides also welcomed the establishment of ApexBrasil office in New Delhi which will strengthen business-to-business linkages and greater flow of Brazilian investment in India. India and Brazil have a long-standing relationship characterised by mutual trust, democratic values, and growing economic engagement. The visit further boosted the momentum in bilateral ties and reaffirmed the shared commitment of both countries towards building a stronger and future-oriented economic partnership

title: Department of Telecommunications Cautions Citizens against IMEI Tampering and Misuse of Telecommunication Identifiers
subtitle:
IMEI Tampering and Telecom Identifier Misuse May Attract Up to Three Years’ Imprisonment and ₹50 Lakh Fine

Citizens advised to use the Sanchar Saathi Portal and Mobile App to verify and secure their mobile connections and handsets
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
With the rapid expansion of mobile connectivity and digital services across India, the misuse of telecommunication identifiers, including the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number of mobile devices, has emerged as a matter of serious concern. Such misuse can compromise the safety of citizens and pose risks to the security and integrity of telecommunication networks. The Government of India has put in place stringent legal provisions to prevent tampering with and misuse of unique telecommunication identifiers.
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) reiterates that tampering with IMEI numbers or using devices with unauthorised or tampered telecommunication identifiers is a punishable offence under the
Telecommunications Act, 2023
and the rules framed thereunder.
Key Legal Provisions
The
Telecommunications Act, 2023
provides for stringent action against tampering with telecommunication identifiers, including the IMEI number of mobile handsets and other telecommunication devices.
Section 42(3)(c)
prohibits tampering with telecommunication identifiers.
Section 42(3)(e)
prohibits obtaining Subscriber Identity Modules (SIMs) or telecommunication identifiers through fraud, cheating or impersonation.
Violations may attract imprisonment for up to
three years
, a fine of up to
₹50 lakh
, or both. Such offences are
cognizable and non-bailable
under
Section 42(7)
of the Act. Under
Section 42(6)
, persons who abet or promote the commission of such offences are also liable to the same punishment.
What Citizens Should Avoid
DoT advises citizens to refrain from:
Using, procuring or assembling devices such as modems, modules, SIM Boxes or other equipment with configurable or tampered IMEIs;
Procuring SIM cards through fake documents, fraud, cheating or impersonation;
Transferring, selling or handing over SIM cards obtained in their name to others who may misuse them; and
Using mobile applications, websites or any other means to modify Calling Line Identity (CLI) or other telecommunication identifiers.
Citizens should also note that procuring SIM cards in their own name and subsequently loaning,  renting or muling of SIM  for misuse in cyber fraud or any other unlawful activity may result in legal liability for the original subscriber.
Using devices with tampered IMEI numbers, obtaining SIM cards through fraudulent means, or transferring SIM cards to persons who misuse them can have serious legal consequences..
Verification and Reporting through Sanchar Saathi
Citizens are encouraged to remain vigilant and make use of the digital tools available through the
Sanchar Saathi
initiative to verify and secure their mobile handsets.
The IMEI details of a mobile handset can be verified through the Sanchar Saathi platform. The service enables citizens to check details such as the brand name, model name and manufacturer information associated with the device.
The Government has put in place robust measures to prevent the misuse of telecommunication resources and strengthen the safety and security of India's telecommunications ecosystem. Citizens can access various services available under the Sanchar Saathi initiative to verify and protect their mobile connections and devices.
Compliance with the provisions of the
Telecommunications Act, 2023
and the rules framed thereunder is essential for preventing telecom-related fraud, protecting citizens and ensuring a safe, secure and trusted telecommunication environment.
Citizens are encouraged to visit the

at

or download the

to access the various citizen-centric services available on the platform.

title: C-DOT Unveils 14 Indigenous Quantum Products to Strengthen Security of India’s Communication Networks
subtitle: Quantum Product Series covers Quantum Key Distribution and Post-Quantum Cryptography solutions for secure and future-ready communications in quantum era
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, unveiled 14 indigenous Quantum Products developed in the areas of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) during its 43rd Foundation Day celebrations in New Delhi.
The products unveiled include:
Q-AKSHAY CD: A compact, fibre-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) system based on Coherent One Way (COW) and Differential Phase Shift (DPS) protocols in a compact 1U size. It enables secure quantum key generation and distribution over fibre networks.
Q-AKSHAY MD: A fibre-based QKD system based on the Measurement Device Independent (MDI) protocol, offering enhanced security against vulnerabilities associated with measurement devices. It represents C-DOT’s next-generation approach to secure quantum key distribution.
C-SPD: A Single-Photon Detector, a critical sub-module used in quantum communication systems.
C-RD: A wideband RF driver designed to drive intensity and phase modulators used in quantum communication systems. It serves as a critical sub-module for enabling high-performance quantum communication applications.
Q-SETU: A quantum-safe encryptor designed to secure Layer 3 communications with a throughput of up to 80 Mbps. It incorporates National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms to protect data against emerging quantum-era threats.
Q-MAHASETU: A next-generation, commercial-grade quantum-safe encryptor supporting Layer 2/3 networks with throughput of up to 40 Gbps. It uses NIST PQC algorithms to provide high-speed, quantum-resistant protection for enterprise and critical communication networks.
Q-VIKRAM: A defence-grade quantum-safe encryptor providing up to 1 Gbps throughput for Layer 2/3 networks. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms to provide enhanced protection for sensitive and strategic communications.
Q-AMOGH: A high-speed quantum-safe optical encryptor providing up to 200 Gbps throughput at Layer 1. Based on NIST PQC algorithms, it is designed to secure high-capacity optical communication links against emerging quantum threats.
Q-DARSHAN: A quantum-safe video IP phone incorporating NIST PQC algorithms to protect voice and video communications. It brings quantum-safe security directly into IP-based communication systems.
Q-VACHAN: A quantum-safe in-line node for IP phones using NIST PQC algorithms. It can upgrade existing IP phones with quantum security.
Q-RAQSHAK: A quantum-safe enterprise network solution designed to protect enterprise communications and network infrastructure. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms to provide protection against current and future cryptographic threats.
Q-VAAYU: A quantum-safe wireless point-to-point network solution designed to secure wireless communication links. It uses NIST PQC algorithms to provide quantum-resistant security for wireless connectivity.
Q-VAJRA1000: A quantum-safe access node designed to upgrade existing communication networks with quantum security. It can support technologies such as GPON and wireless radios, enabling quantum-safe protection to be integrated into existing network infrastructure.
Q-PARAKRAM: A defence-grade quantum-safe encryptor providing up to 1 Gbps throughput for Layer 2/3 networks. It incorporates NIST PQC algorithms and other proprietary algorithms and is designed to provide robust quantum-resistant security for strategic and defence communications.
The Quantum Product Series brings together solutions for quantum-safe encryption, secure communications and critical components for quantum communication systems, catering to enterprise, telecom, wireless, optical, strategic and defence applications.The Quantum Product Series combines QKD technologies and PQC-based solutions to enable secure quantum key generation and distribution and are designed to protect communications against threats posed by future quantum computers. The quantum portfolio from C-DOT also spans specialised quantum communication components that can go in building quantum-safe security solutions for existing and next-generation networks by the eco system working in this area.
The products reflect the Centre’s focus on translating indigenous research and innovation into deployable solutions for securing India’s communication infrastructure in the emerging quantum era. These products have been developed to address emerging cybersecurity challenges associated with the advent of quantum computing and to strengthen the security and resilience of India’s communication networks.
A Quantum Product Series booklet, consolidating C-DOT’s indigenous quantum solutions, was also launched by the dignitaries. The booklet presents C-DOT’s work in QKD and PQC and highlights its efforts towards developing secure, resilient and future-ready communication technologies. Follow the link to access booklet:

content:
The Indian Navy commissioned INS Nipun, the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV) of the Nistar Class, at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai, on 31 Aug 2026, marking a significant enhancement of the Navy’s deep-sea diving, underwater intervention and submarine rescue capabilities.
The commissioning ceremony was presided over by Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, in the presence of Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command
. Senior naval officers, representatives from Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam, veterans, distinguished guests and families of the commissioning crew were also in attendance.
Indigenously designed and constructed by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam
, INS Nipun is a significant addition to the Indian Navy’s specialist underwater capability. Her induction demonstrates India’s growing capability to design and build technologically complex specialist naval platforms and is another significant step towards
Aatmanirbharta
in defence shipbuilding. It also reflects the contribution of Indian shipyards, domestic industry and associated agencies towards strengthening the Navy’s indigenous capability.
INS Nipun is a purpose-built platform designed primarily for deep-sea diving and underwater operations. The ship is capable of
supporting saturation, air and heliox diving
and is equipped with remotely operated underwater systems for inspection and intervention. Her specialised diving complex, dynamic positioning capability and associated life-support and medical facilities enable sustained and complex operations at sea.
INS Nipun is also capable of
supporting submarine rescue operations,
significantly strengthening the Indian Navy’s ability to respond to underwater contingencies. Along with her sister ship INS Nistar, the ship substantially enhances the Navy’s specialist capability in diving, underwater intervention, salvage and submarine rescue.
The ship’s crest and motto embody the spirit of her specialised role and the men who venture into the depths. The motto,
‘Far Beneath, Few Beyond’,
reflects the resolve, skill and endurance required to operate in one of the most challenging domains of the maritime environment.
In his address, CNS stated that the induction of INS Nipun reflects the seamless synergy between the Indian Navy, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and the domestic industrial network. He further stated that proving the role-worthiness of all diving systems during sea trials in a single sortie stands as a testament to the nation’s technical confidence and engineering prowess.
CNS emphasised that combat readiness remains the Indian Navy’s highest priority amidst an increasingly contested maritime environment and growing threats to global maritime highways. He noted that, based on the West Coast under the Western Naval Command, INS Nipun will be a powerful addition to the specialised underwater capabilities required to sustain multi-domain operations.
The CNS highlighted that the niche capabilities of INS Nipun, available with only a handful of global navies, enable a swift response to distressed submarines of the Indian Navy as well as partner nations. This capability positions India as the
‘Preferred Submarine Rescue Partner’
in the region, while also providing specialised support for underwater salvage and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions.
Addressing the commissioning crew, CNS stated that they inherit not just a sophisticated platform, but also the onerous responsibility to shape the ship’s soul and instil spirit into her steel. Exhorting the crew to live up to the ship’s motto of
‘
Nischay, Nirbhay, Nipun
’ (Resolve, Fearlessness and Professional Mastery),
he urged them to remain anchored in the core naval values of
Duty, Honour and Courage.
With the hoisting of the Commissioning Pennant, INS Nipun has formally entered operational service with the Indian Navy, ready to support those who operate beneath the waves and contribute to safeguarding India’s maritime interests.

title: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw addressed media on Semicon 2.0
subtitle:
Notifications for all 6 Pillars of Semicon 2.0 issued

India achieved target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers in four years against 10-year target: Ashwini Vaishnaw

Close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market will be in India in the coming years: Ashwini Vaishnaw

Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have designed more than 250 semiconductor chips: Ashwini Vaishnaw
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways and Information & Broadcasting, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, today addressed the media and outlined the Government’s vision for taking India’s semiconductor ecosystem to the next level. On the occasion, notifications for all six pillars of the Semicon 2.0 Scheme were issued, marking a significant step towards strengthening India’s semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities.
The scheme builds on the momentum generated by the first Semicon India Programme and provides fiscal and infrastructure support across the semiconductor value chain from chip design, fabrication and packaging to equipment, materials, research and development, and talent development.
The scheme aims to strengthen India’s economic growth and national security by improving semiconductor supply-chain resilience and establishing technological leadership in critical sectors. It will operate through six pillars covering 10 categories.
The six pillars under Semicon 2.0 are:
• Pillar 1 -  Design
• Pillar 2 - Machines and Materials
• Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs
• Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry
• Pillar 5 - Research and Development
• Pillar 6 - Talent Development
Pillar 1 - Design: Categories: Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips, System-on-Chips (SoCs), and Modules for National Importance and Strategic Priorities; Design of Semiconductor IPs, Chips and SoCs for the Commercial Sector; and Deployment-Linked Incentive (DLI) for Semiconductor IPs/Chips/SoCs for deployment.
Pillar 2  - Machines and Materials: Category: Semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
Pillar 3 - Setting up more Fabs: Categories: Silicon Semiconductor Wafer Fabs; Compound Semiconductors/Photonics/Sensors (including MEMS) Fab/Discrete Semiconductors Fab; and Display Fabs.
Pillar 4 - Further strengthening the ATMP/OSAT industry: Category: Semiconductor Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) / Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) Facility.
Pillar 5  -  Research and Development: Category: R&D for advanced semiconductor technologies.
Pillar 6  -  Talent Development: Category: Talent Development.
During the event Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said “India achieved its target of developing 85,000 semiconductor engineers over a period of 10 years in just four years, and has now set a new target of developing one lakh more engineers. In the coming years, close to 10% of the global semiconductor industry’s market is expected to be in India. Students from Tier-II and Tier-III cities have already designed more than 250 chips. In one case, commercial production commenced within just 13 months of the groundbreaking, while approvals were granted within 200 days, 150 days and even 90 days in multiple cases. The semiconductor ecosystem being developed in India is also expected to create 50,000–60,000 direct jobs.”
Projects supported under Semicon 2.0 will generally have a duration of up to six years, while the scheme will initially remain open for applications for three years.
The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) will be the nodal agency for Semicon 2.0. It will invite applications, undertake technical and financial appraisal, recommend applicants and oversee implementation. ISM may implement the design and deployment categories with the assistance of C-DAC. The mission may also announce semiconductor deep-tech awards from 2026 to promote niche innovation.
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology will make budgetary provisions for fiscal support, with disbursements undertaken by the nodal agency in accordance with approved conditions. A mid-term assessment will be conducted after three years of implementation, or as required, to evaluate the scheme’s impact and consider modifications or continuation.

title: 4th Indo-German Environment Forum to be held in New Delhi on September 1, 2026
subtitle: Forum to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation and Facilitate Multi-Stakeholder Exchange on Environment and Climate Change
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with German Minister for Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety H.E. Carsten Schneider, will co-chair the 4th Indo-German Environment Forum, themed 'Together For More Resilience', in New Delhi on 01.09.2026.
The Indo-German Environment Forum is the highest-level bilateral forum between India and Germany on environmental policy and has been held since 2008. It is being jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, and the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN), Germany, in association with the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA) and Indian industry associations.
Shri Yadav and H.E. Schneider will discuss key issues relating to environmental protection and climate policy to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, exchange experiences and advance practical collaboration. Through thematic sessions, the Forum will focus on challenges, solutions and opportunities in the areas of Low-Carbon Industries; Biodiversity in Wetlands, Mountains and Forests; Resource Efficiency & Circular Economy as a Business Model; and Sustainable Finance, Green Skills and Investment Mobilization.
The Forum will provide a platform for bilateral exchanges among policymakers, private-sector representatives, think tanks and other key stakeholders on environmental and climate cooperation between the two countries. Representatives from ministries, businesses, expert groups and non-governmental organisations will participate in the Forum.
Ahead of the Forum, the three Joint Working Groups on Climate Change, Biodiversity and Circular Economy met this year. The respective working groups discussed the progress made and areas of mutual interest.
The Forum assumes significance in the context of the strong and growing economic and industrial linkages between India and Germany and the potential for deeper cooperation in sustainable technologies and the green economy.

title: DRI seizes over 42 kg foreign-origin gold worth more than RS. 65 crore in crackdown on gold smuggling
subtitle: 25 persons arrested in multiple intelligence-led operations across Kolkata, Mumbai, Kerala and other locations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 9:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has, in a series of intelligence-led operations across the country in recent days, seized over
42 kg foreign-origin gold, and around 10 kg Silver
, collectively valued at more than Rs. 65 crore, and
arrested 25 persons including 5 foreign nationals.
The operations have exposed diverse and sophisticated modus operandi, including concealment in specially fabricated vehicle cavities, body concealment, use of transit passengers and airport personnel, and smuggling through land and coastal routes.
Major operation at Mumbai Airport
On 28/29.08.26, DRI unearthed a well-organised syndicate involved in smuggling foreign-origin gold through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai. The syndicate involved foreign nationals transiting through Mumbai from destinations including Dubai, Bangkok and Male, as well as an airport staff member facilitating clandestine removal of the smuggled gold at Mumbai. A total of
16 capsules containing 6.85 kg of 24-carat gold dust in wax form
, were recovered and seized.
6.85 kg gold in wax form seized at Mumbai airport
The operation resulted in the arrest of
six persons
, comprising of five foreign nationals who were transiting through Mumbai and one airport staff member. The operation once again highlights that organised networks are increasingly exploiting transit routes and airport personnel for clandestine removal of smuggled gold.
Major seizures in Kolkata/West Bengal
On 29,08,26, in two separate intelligence-led operations at NSCBI Airport, Kolkata, officers of DRI intercepted two passengers travelling from Bangkok and Dubai respectively, suspected to be part of gold-smuggling syndicates.
15.61 kg gold seized by DRI in coordination with BSF in Nadia district
In a case involving two passengers coming from Dubai,
4.87 kg gold
was recovered after semi-solid gold-containing paste was found concealed in the undergarments and jeans of two passengers. The material was melted and the extracted gold in bar form was seized.
Both passengers were arrested
under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
In another case, involving flight coming from Bangkok,
3.36 kg foreign-origin gold
was recovered in the form of 11 raw chains from one passenger, which had allegedly been handed over to him by the second passenger for crossing the Green Channel. Both passengers were arrested.
On the same day, in another case, the DRI seized
125 pieces of foreign-origin gold bars weighing 15.61 kg
. It was
recovered by troops of Border Security Force (BSF), at BOP Tungi from a woman during a surprise search of her residential premise in Banpur village, Nadia district.  During investigation by DRI, the woman admitted to her involvement in the alleged smuggling activity along with the men of the house. The woman was arrested
under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
1.74 kg gold seized by DRI in coordination with BSF
Two more seizures in Kerala
In two separate operations in Kerala on 29.08.2026, DRI Cochin Zonal Unit and its Calicut Regional Unit intercepted passengers arriving from Ras Al Khaimah and Jeddah respectively. At Cochin International Airport,
1.78 kg gold
, was extracted from two packets of gold in compound form concealed on the person of a passenger arriving from Ras Al Khaimah; the passenger was arrested.
At Calicut International Airport, DRI officers, along with the Air Intelligence Unit, detected
549 grams of 24-carat foreign-origin gold
, concealed in especially created cavities inside the heavy alloy portion of an iron box carried by a passenger arriving from Jeddah. The gold was seized under the Customs Act,1962 and the passenger was arrested.
Earlier in the week, on 26–27.08.2026, DRI, in coordination with BSF, also effected several significant seizures of foreign-origin gold along the Indo-Bangladesh border, The officers of DRI Unit seized
935 grams
and
1.74 kg
foreign-origin gold in two separate operations, resulting in the arrest of one person in each case.
In another operation in Kolkata,
1.48 kg foreign-origin (FO) gold in paste form
, allegedly smuggled from Thailand, was recovered by officers of DRI from four persons.  who were found to be carrying smuggled FO Gold in paste form in 5 capsules secreted in their rectum/ body during aa domestic road trip. All four persons and their handler were arrested.
In Guwahati, DRI seized
3.84 kg foreign-origin gold bars
allegedly smuggled through the Indo-Bangladesh border in the Tripura sector and arrested two persons including a lady.
Further, in Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu, DRI seized
1.360 kg foreign-origin gold and 9.99 kg foreign-origin silver
, allegedly smuggled through the coastal route from Sri Lanka, and arrested three persons.
Seized gold and silver at  Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu
DRI's intelligence-led and coordinated enforcement actions continue to disrupt these networks at multiple stages of the smuggling chain and prevent the illicit movement of precious metals into the country.

title: NPCI International and Uzbekistan’s NIPC Partner to Enable UPI Payments Across Uzbekistan via UZQR
subtitle:
Indian tourists, business travellers and students can make instant merchant payments by scanning Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code, UZQR

Partnership between NIPL and Uzbekistan’s National payment system marks a significant step in expanding UPI’s international footprint
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
NPCI International Payments Ltd. (NIPL), the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), has entered into a commercial agreement with the National Interbank Processing Centre JSC (NIPC), operator of Uzbekistan’s national payment system, HUMO, on 30th August 2026. The partnership enables Indian travellers to scan Uzbekistan’s national interoperable QR code UZQR using their familiar UPI-enabled applications to make instant merchant payments across the country.
The announcement was made during the bilateral visit of the Prime Minister of India to Uzbekistan. The execution of the agreement follows formal approvals from financial regulators, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (CBU), which designated HUMO as NIPL’s authorised partner for cross-border merchant acceptance.
Key Highlights of the Agreement
Universal Merchant Acceptance:
By integrating with CBU’s mandated Unified National QR infrastructure (UZQR), UPI users gain near-universal acceptance across retail, hospitality, and service merchants in Uzbekistan.
Seamless Travel Experience:
Indian tourists, business travellers, and students can make direct person-to-merchant (P2M) payments from their Indian bank accounts, eliminating foreign exchange markup friction and reducing reliance on international cards or cash.
Strengthened Bilateral Ties:
The initiative advances digital public infrastructure cooperation and aligns with both nations' broader strategic and economic goals.
UPI is Accepted in Ten Countries
Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece, enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI.

title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj to launch fisheries Infrastructure projects worth Rs 36.49 Crore
subtitle: Major Focus on Strengthening Fisheries Infrastructure to Boost the Fisheries Value Chain and create better livelihoods opportunities
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:

content:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India is organizing a launch of Fisheries Infrastructure Project under PMMSY and Multi-Dimensional Capacity Building Conclave for Co-operative Led Seaweed Farming under Blue Economy on 1st September 2026, at Kamarajar Manimadapam, Puducherry to strengthen fisheries infrastructure, promote sustainable livelihood opportunities for coastal communities, enhance value chain efficiencies and accelerate the development through a cooperative-led approach.
The Outreach Programme will be graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Shri K. Kailashnathan, Hon'ble Lieutenant Governor, Puducherry, Thiru N. Rangasamy, Hon'ble Chief Minister, Puducherry, Thiru A. Anbalagan, Hon'ble Speaker, Puducherry Legislative Assembly, Shri Malladi Krishna Rao, Hon'ble Fisheries Minister, Puducherry, Shri G. N. S. Rajasekaran, Hon'ble Agriculture Minister, Puducherry, Shri A. Namassivayam, Hon'ble Home Minister, Puducherry, A. John Kumaradhas, Hon'ble Chief Minister's Adviser, V. P. Sivakolundhu, Hon'ble Civil Supplies Minister, Puducherry, Shri V. Vaithilingam, Hon'ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Puducherry, Shri S. Selvaganabathy, Hon'ble Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), Puducherry, Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of India and Dr Sharat Chauhan,
Chief Secretary, Government of Puducherry
The event will also witness the participation of fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Puducherry and representatives from fisheries
value chain stakeholders.
Puducherry is emerging as a model for sustainable and infrastructure-led fisheries development under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Blessed with rich marine resources and a vibrant fishing community, the Union Territory has witnessed significant investments in modern fisheries infrastructure, including the upgradation of the Thengaithittu Fishing Harbour and the establishment of a state-of-the-art Fish Landing Centre at Nallavadu. These facilities have enhanced fish handling, berthing, auctioning and safety arrangements, benefiting thousands of fishers and over 600 fishing families in the coastal region. Puducherry is also pioneering cooperative-led seaweed farming through the Advanced Centre for Innovation and Capacity Development (ACICD) at Karaikal, which leverages modern technologies and promotes sustainable livelihoods, particularly for fisherwomen. Together, these initiatives are strengthening the fisheries value chain, generating employment, enhancing incomes and advancing the vision of a prosperous Blue Economy in the Union Territory.
Further strengthening this momentum, the government of India has taken a Cluster approach for strengthening the fisheries value chain notifying Karaikal in Puducherry as a Fishing Harbour Cluster under PMMSY and a Smart and Integrated Fishing Harbour is also being developed in Karaikal with a total outlay of Rs. 119.94 Crore. The modern facility will enable safe vessel berthing, hygienic fish handling and efficient marketing, while improving operational efficiency, strengthening the fisheries value chain and creating better livelihood opportunities for coastal communities.
This integrated approach will support the focused development of Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs) and fisheries cooperatives by strengthening their institutional capacity and improving access to modern infrastructure, finance, technology, value addition and markets. By enabling collective action and greater participation across the fisheries value chain, the initiative will help sustainably harness Puducherry’s untapped fisheries potential, enhance incomes and generate new livelihood opportunities for coastal communities.

title: Hon’ble Vice-President of India attends Fisheries Outreach Programme in Agatti, Lakshadweep to Strengthen India’s Blue Economy
subtitle: Major focus on Sustainably Harnessing the Untapped Potential of high value Island Resources including Tuna, Seaweed and Ornamental fisheries
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 2:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India organized
Fisheries
Outreach Programme
of Ministry of Fisheries, Govt. of India at
Agatti, Lakshadweep
on
31st August 2026
. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has given special focus to strengthening fisheries farmer producer organizations (FFPO) and fisheries cooperatives while sustainably harnessing high value species like tuna, seaweed and Ornamental fisheries resources. The Hon’ble Vice President also released “
Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031
” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development.
The Outreach Programme was graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj along with Shri Praful Khode Patel, Hon’ble Administrator of Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Dius. The event also witnessed the participation of fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Lakshadweep, representatives from fisheries cluster and line Ministries and Departments.
The Hon’ble Vice President of India,
Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan
, described Lakshadweep as a priceless maritime asset of the nation and highlighted its immense fisheries potential, supported by a 4,200 sq. km lagoon area and an Exclusive Economic Zone of nearly 4 lakh sq. km. He noted that the outreach programme reflected the collective commitment of the Government of India, Lakshadweep Administration, scientific institutions and fishing communities towards ushering in a new era of sustainable growth and prosperity through the Blue Economy. Referring to fisheries and aquaculture as a sunrise sector of the economy, he appreciated the approval of fisheries development projects worth over ₹62 crore under PMMSY for Lakshadweep. The Vice President also highlighted the enabling framework announced by the Government for sustainable harvesting of fisheries resources from the EEZ and High Seas, stating that it would empower fishers to responsibly access deep-sea resources and benefit from new opportunities. He emphasized that Lakshadweep possesses an estimated fisheries potential of over 1 lakh tonnes, including about 94,000 tonnes of tuna and tuna-like species, and underscored the importance of scientific harvesting, digital authorization systems, vessel monitoring, international certification and sustainable fishing practices to enhance fishers’ incomes and strengthen India’s position in global seafood markets. He further stressed that conservation of marine resources and adherence to responsible fishing practices are essential for ensuring long-term prosperity of the fisheries sector and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
During the event, the Hon’ble Vice President distributed Benefits to beneficiaries under PMMSY which included support for acquisition of Deep-Sea Fishing Vessels (DSFVs) for traditional fishermen, promotion of recreational fisheries aligned with the tourism potential of the islands, provision of safety kits for traditional and motorised fishing vessels, facilitation of Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) for fishermen, assistance for replacement of old fishing boats and nets, and supply of communication and tracking devices. The beneficiaries included Mr. Haleema K Cheriyadam, President, Malsyam Fishermen Cooperative Society Ltd, Androth Island; Private Entrepreneurs namely Mr. Althaf Munavver Tanveer, Mr. Noor Mohammed, Mr. Ameen Bin Mohammed C N; Boat owners namely Mr. Sadik S, Mr. Noushad Khan Nasheeda Mahal, Mr. Ashik, Mr. Kidave Kunhikadiyapada, and fichermen namely, Mr. Aboobacker Uriyoda, and Mr. Sabeeh Mubarak
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh
, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, stated that the outreach programme reflects the Government’s commitment to understanding the needs of Lakshadweep’s fishing communities and preparing a comprehensive roadmap for enhancing fishers’ incomes, strengthening infrastructure, improving safety at sea, promoting value addition and expanding market access
.
He highlighted the transformational initiatives undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, including the Blue Revolution, FIDF, PMMSY and PMMKSSY, which have significantly accelerated the growth of the fisheries sector. The Minister noted that India’s fish production has increased from 95.7 lakh tonnes in 2013-14 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, while seafood exports have witnessed substantial growth reaching a record Rs. 73,890 Crore in 2025-26 despite trade challenges. Emphasizing Lakshadweep’s vast untapped high value tuna resources, he underscored the need to sustainably harness the island resources to create new livelihood opportunities for fishers, cooperatives, FPOs and women-led enterprises. He further highlighted the Government’s policy initiatives, including the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the Exclusive Economic Zone Rules, 2025 and the Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas, 2025, which provide an enabling framework for responsible offshore fisheries development including the launch of Access pass and Letter of Authorization under the same.
Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel
, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj, highlighted Lakshadweep’s strategic importance in India’s Blue Economy, noting that although small in land area, the islands account for nearly 17% of India’s Exclusive Economic Zone. He stated that the Government is working towards securing international sustainability certification and developing a global “Lakshadweep Sustainable Tuna” brand to enhance export competitiveness and fishers’ incomes. The Minister further informed that Lakshadweep has been notified as a Seaweed Cluster and that a Seaweed Bank has been approved in collaboration with ICAR-CMFRI. He noted that 575 seaweed cultivation units, supported by an investment of about ₹2 crore, are being promoted to generate livelihood opportunities for women, youth and self-help groups. Highlighting the potential of ornamental fisheries, he stated that Lakshadweep is home to over 300 ornamental fish species and that an ornamental fish hatchery has been established at Agatti, while three rearing units have been approved under PMMSY. He also noted that 19 recreational fishing units have been sanctioned under PMMSY to promote fisheries-based tourism and create additional income opportunities for island communities.
Shri Praful Khoda Patel
, Hon’ble Administrator of Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu., highlighted the immense untapped fisheries potential of the islands, noting that against an estimated annual fisheries potential of nearly 1 lakh metric tonnes, particularly of high-value Yellowfin and Skipjack Tuna, the current harvest stands at only about 15,000 metric tonnes. He emphasized that the Government is taking determined steps to bridge this gap through targeted interventions in tuna fisheries, deep-sea fishing, seaweed cultivation and fish processing. He informed that under the support of the Government of India, 16 Deep Sea Fishing Vessels, each costing about ₹1.2 crore, have been sanctioned for fishers with full financial assistance, and their construction is already underway. The Administrator further highlighted the vast potential for seaweed farming across the islands and stated that new initiatives in fisheries infrastructure, value addition and processing, along with the upcoming fisheries policy of Lakshadweep, are expected to create substantial livelihood opportunities and significantly enhance the incomes of local fishers. He expressed confidence that Lakshadweep would emerge as a model region for fisheries-led Blue Economy development in the coming years.
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi
, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, highlighted that Lakshadweep occupies a strategic position in India’s fisheries and aquaculture landscape, with the island territories of Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar together accounting for nearly 50% of the country’s Exclusive Economic Zone. He noted that the resource-rich waters surrounding the islands offer immense opportunities for tuna fisheries, deep-sea fishing, mariculture, seaweed cultivation and ornamental fisheries.  He noted that the Government has created an enabling framework for sustainable offshore fisheries through the EEZ Rules, 2025 and High Seas Guidelines, 2025, while extending substantial support under PMMSY. He further stated that the establishment of a Seaweed Bank and notification of Lakshadweep as a Seaweed Cluster will create new livelihood opportunities and boost the blue economy, with a continued focus on enhancing fishers’ incomes, skills, safety, market access and adoption of modern technologies.
The Government is strengthening Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs) and fisheries cooperatives through financial, technical and capacity-building support to enable island communities to sustainably harness high-value resources such as tuna and tuna-like species, seaweed, ornamental fisheries and deep-sea fisheries. These interventions aim to improve aggregation, value addition, market access and income opportunities for fishers and other fisheries stakeholders.
Background
India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.
Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework for sustainable harnessing of fisheries from the Indian EEZ and the High Seas including Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025.
Lakshadweep is endowed with rich oceanic fisheries resources, particularly high-value tuna species such as Yellowfin Tuna and Skipjack Tuna, which form the backbone of the island’s marine fisheries sector. Supported by vast and productive waters, these commercially important species offer significant opportunities for sustainable harvesting, value addition, export growth and livelihood generation, positioning Lakshadweep as a key hub for tuna-based fisheries and blue economy development.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Reviews Progress of Rural Health Training Centre, Najafgarh
subtitle: Directs time-bound completion of ongoing works and further strengthening of clinical, academic and training infrastructure
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda today chaired a review meeting to assess the progress of the Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC), Najafgarh, and reviewed the implementation of initiatives aimed at strengthening patient care, infrastructure, manpower, academic activities and digital health systems at the Centre.
Reviewing the progress since the meeting held on April 13, 2026, Shri Nadda directed all concerned agencies and institutions to ensure timely completion of ongoing works and coordinated implementation of planned interventions. He emphasised close monitoring of deliverables, timely availability of manpower and equipment, and continued focus on quality patient care and medical training.
The Centre’s OPD and Emergency services are fully operational, along with the Anti-Rabies Vaccination Centre, Anti-Snake Venom Centre and other supporting facilities viz., Jan Aushadhi Kendra, CSSD, laboratory and ambulance services. The Minor Operation Theatre is functional.
RHTC Najafgarh has also been onboarded onto MedLeapR, for medico-legal cases, and onto PM-JAY under Ayushman Bharat, facilitating access to services for eligible beneficiaries.  RHTC is progressing towards NQAS certification of its UPHCs and development of Model PHCs.
On an average monthly basis, RHTC recorded around 47,000 OPD consultations and 9,000 emergency attendances, besides 221 minor procedures done in August, 2026. TB symptom screening has been integrated into routine OPD and PHC interactions under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.
RHTC is collaborating with other Central Government institutions including Safdarjung Hospital, ABVIMS, Dr. RML Hospital and NIMR for strengthening clinical manpower, training, digital systems, procurement and research. The Centre has also joined the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative.

title: PM Modi’s Viksit Bharat Vision: India Must Build a Future-Ready Workforce for a Global Automotive Industry

Auto Industry Must Drive the Skilling Push as India Emerges as a Global Automotive Hub: H.D. Kumaraswamy

43 Candidates Flagged Off for Romania as India Expands Global Opportunities for Skilled Youth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy on Monday underlined the need to make skilling, upskilling and employment generation for India’s younger generation a central priority as the country moves towards Viksit Bharat @2047, stressing that India’s skilled workforce must be prepared not only to meet domestic requirements but also the growing needs of industries across the world.
Addressing the Automotive Skills Development Council (ASDC) Annual Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, the Union Minister said India’s automotive sector is entering a new era of transformation, driven by electric mobility, automation, connected technologies, advanced manufacturing and Industry 4.0.
Highlighting the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Kumaraswamy said India is steadily moving beyond being merely a large automotive market and is emerging as a major global centre for automotive manufacturing, technology and mobility solutions.
“India’s ambition should not be limited to meeting our domestic manpower requirements. We must aspire to make India a global source of skilled automotive talent.”
The Minister emphasised that the rapid transformation of the automotive industry would require a workforce capable of adapting to new technologies and evolving workplace requirements. He said the focus must extend beyond simply training candidates to ensuring that young people acquire skills that translate into meaningful employment opportunities.
“Creating greater employment opportunities by skilling and upskilling our younger generation is essential not only for India, but for the entire world.”
He said the growing adoption of electric mobility, automation and advanced automotive technologies is creating new employment opportunities across vehicle manufacturing, battery production, charging infrastructure, servicing and after-sales support. This, he added, makes it imperative to develop technicians, engineers and professionals with specialised and industry-relevant capabilities.
Stronger Industry-Skill Linkage
Kumaraswamy stressed that the responsibility for building this workforce cannot rest with skilling institutions alone. Automobile manufacturers, component manufacturers, dealerships and other industry stakeholders will have a major role to play in defining the skills required for the future and ensuring that training reflects real-world requirements
“Skilling cannot succeed in isolation from the workplace. Industry participation is essential to ensure that training reflects real-world requirements and keeps pace with emerging technologies.”
He called for a stronger and more seamless relationship between education, skills and employment, with curricula, training methods and assessment systems continuously updated in consultation with industry.
The Minister said automobile manufacturers must actively participate in this process and help create a talent pipeline capable of meeting the requirements of an increasingly technology-driven industry.
“We need to build a stronger and more seamless relationship between education, skills and employment. Our skilling ecosystem must evolve alongside the growth and transformation of the automotive industry.”
ASDC’s Role in Building a Global Talent Pool
Kumaraswamy said institutions such as ASDC have an important role in ensuring that India’s workforce remains aligned with the changing requirements of the automotive sector.
He said ASDC must continue to work closely with industry to anticipate future requirements and equip young Indians with skills that are relevant both domestically and internationally.
The Minister said India should look beyond creating a workforce merely for its own requirements and position itself as a global supplier of skilled automotive professionals.
“Our responsibility is not merely to create certified candidates, but to create professionals who can contribute to India’s automotive growth and compete at global standards.”
He also underlined the importance of continuous upskilling and reskilling, particularly as new technologies rapidly change the nature of jobs in the automotive sector.
43 Candidates Flagged Off for Romania
During the programme, Kumaraswamy launched the ASDC Annual Report and flagged off 43 candidates placed in Romania, highlighting the growing international opportunities available to skilled Indian youth.
The Minister said such opportunities demonstrate how India’s investment in skills can create pathways for young Indians to participate in the global workforce.
The ASDC’s work is already expanding significantly. During FY 2025–26, the council impacted 5,08,173 learners, conducted 1,53,240 assessments and generated 2,88,756 apprenticeship contracts across approximately 3,700 establishments.
With the automotive industry undergoing a fundamental technological transformation, Kumaraswamy said the partnership between government, industry, academia and skilling institutions must become stronger.
“India has the ambition, the market and the manufacturing opportunity. Our collective responsibility is to ensure that we also have the skilled workforce capable of delivering on that ambition.”
He said the government would continue to support initiatives that strengthen manufacturing capabilities, promote technology adoption and develop the skills required for the industries of the future.
“A future-ready India requires a future-ready workforce. Through skilling, upskilling and strong industry participation, we can create opportunities for our youth in India and across the world.”
The Union Minister concluded by stressing that India’s demographic strength can become one of its greatest economic assets if the country succeeds in equipping its younger generation with the right skills and connecting those skills to employment opportunities.

title: Mission Zero: Depalpur Triumphs in Tackling Legacy Waste
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indore has taken Depalpur under its wing. From successfully implementing the rigorous 4-bin waste segregation system to clearing out 1,250 tons of legacy waste, the transformation is nothing short of incredible!
MoHUA stepped up capacity building, peer-learning with Swachh Shehar Jodi, launched during Swachhata Hi Seva 2025. 72 mentor cities and 200 mentee cities have undertaken 1600 + activities in the urban waste management sector. This 100 day intervention is based on the Each One Teach One model and is the largest time-bound and structured mentorship framework in urban waste management programme under SBM-U. Mentor and mentee cities have signed MoUs to foster knowledge transfer, peer learning, and replication of best practices. Cities are currently undertaking field visits and addressing gaps in SWM and UWM keeping in mind best practices being shared by the mentor cities.
Depalpur’s journey to “Zero Legacy Waste”, reads like a triumph of collective will and scientific precision, under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0. Under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, Indore Municipal Corporation and Depalpur Nagar Parishad worked hand in hand to build a people‑driven waste management system. Door‑to‑door collection and segregation into four categories, has now become routine. Once 100% coverage was achieved, the focus shifted to the daunting challenge of legacy waste.
The historic Surajkund Bawdi has been revived, streets are covered in vibrant wall art, and plastic-free zones are the new normal. Meanwhile, Indore continues its own grassroots upgrades with the inspiring 'Basti Bemisal' slum-transformation campaign.
Under the leadership of Mayor Shri Pushyamitra Bhargav and Commissioner IAS Kshitij Singhal, Depalpur achieved the complete remediation of its dumpsite, remediating 1,250 metric tonnes of waste that had accumulated over 5 years.
The scale of the operation in Depalpur was nothing short of remarkable. Over 500 ragpickers from Indore Municipal Corporation were mobilized, working shoulder to shoulder with Depalpur Nagar Parishad’s heavy machinery - dumpers, JCBs, and loaders - to dismantle years of accumulated waste. The process was meticulously planned: waste was segregated at the site into distinct streams, ensuring that every fraction was channelled to its rightful destination. From this effort, 4.5 tonnes of recyclables like plastic, metal, and glass, were recovered and sold to authorized recyclers, while 50–60 tonnes of Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) were transported to the NEPRA plant in Indore, shredded, and then dispatched to cement factories for co‑processing. This seamless chain of collection, segregation, scientific processing, and authorized channelization reflected discipline, efficiency, and a commitment to sustainability.
When remediation was declared complete, the dumpsite was no longer a scar on the landscape but a canvas for renewal. A plantation drive was launched, with 200 saplings planted by officials and public representatives, symbolizing the rebirth of the land. The community gathered for a celebratory “Poha Party,” a gesture that turned the achievement into a shared moment of pride and ownership. Looking ahead, the site is set to evolve into a vibrant public space, envisioned as a hub for cricket matches, citizen engagement programs, and social gatherings like “Tiffin Party.” What was once a mound of waste is now poised to become a green, lively ground for community life, Depalpur’s testament to how determination and collective action can transform a dumpsite into a landmark of civic triumph. Depalpur has thus become the first city under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative to achieve “Zero Legacy Waste.” It is not just a milestone in sanitation but a story of how leadership, planning, and community participation can erase a dumpsite and replace it with green promise and civic pride.
